newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam says Petronas oil announcement premature.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam says Petronas oil announcement premature.

text.p: A senior Petrovietnam official said on Tuesday an announcement by Malaysia's Petronas that it had acquired a stake in Vietnam's Dai Hung oil project from Australia's Broken Hill Propriety Co. Ltd was premature.

"It's too early... It's not news," said Do Van Ha, chief international negotiator for Petrovietnam. "They need to submit any necessary document to Petrovietnam for review and approval and then submit it to the government for a modified business licence."
Ha added that pending completion of any transfer agreement BHP remained the operator and was therefore required to fulfill its obligations and liabilities in accordance with its contract.
"Any changes to a partner's working interests... will need to have MPI (Ministry of Planning and Investment) approval," he said.
A spokesman in Kuala Lumpur for Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) told Reuters earlier on Tuesday that the firm had acquired a 43.75 percent stake in the offshore field from BHP.
Press reports in Australia said the deal had been completed in principle by the two parties and was awaiting government ratification in Hanoi.
But industry executives in Hanoi said final approval by the Vietnamese government was likely to take time and might not prove simple.
Petronas already owns a 20 percent stake in Dai Hung. The additional 43.75 percent stake would make it the largest shareholder in the field.

According to initial estimates Dai Hung had recoverable oil reserves of 700 million barrels, but this was later revised down to 100 million barrels, prompting BHP to seek revisions to its Production Sharing Contract.
